notes.claim: An inverse function is the original function in reverse; for a function that multiplies by 3 and subtracts one, the inverse adds one and then divides by 3.
Not all functions have an inverse; only one-to-one functions do.
A horizontal line cutting a graph more than once, as it does for y = x², shows a many-to-one function, which by the rule above has no inverse.
The SQA HN Engineering Mathematics unit includes determining inverse functions of a range of functions and graphing functions with their inverses.

sources.title: About the HELM Project
sources.quote: We see that a horizontal line drawn on the graph cuts it more than once. This means that two (or more) different inputs have yielded the same output and so the function is many-to-one.

sources.title: Higher – Functions – GCSE Maths Revision – BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: For example, for a function that multiplies by 3 and subtracts one , the inverse function is add one and then divide by 3 .
